children: The Federal Aviation Administration has ordered a ground stop at airports across the country "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the ground stop was "a telecommunication outage." He added, "this isn't a safety to the American people or another 9/11."

Shares of airline stocks fell in after-hours trading, with American, Delta, Southwest, and United all down between 1% and 2%. JetBlue fell more than 3%. Meanwhile, shares of rental car company Hertz shot up 10%, with Avis up 4%, possibly because travelers are looking for alternate transportation options while departures are halted.
American Airlines said that flights already in transit can continue to their destinations and that they expected schedule disruptions through the end of the day.
Flight-tracking site Flight Aware reported that more than 9,000 flights had been delayed into or out of the United States today.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote on X that the stoppage was due to "a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Center." He added that "FAA technicians are investigating the issue."

By 5:30 p.m. Eastern time, the agency's National Airspace Systems Status dashboard reported ground stops at New York's JFK airport, as well as at airports in Las Vegas, Newark, Philadelphia, and Seattle.
